questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the veto power in the UN Security Council?

options.A: Each of the five permanent members can block the adoption of a substantive resolution by voting against it
options.B: Any member of the Security Council can block a resolution by voting against it
options.C: The Secretary-General can veto any resolution
options.D: A veto requires the support of at least three permanent members

questions.explanation: Each of the five permanent members can block the adoption of a substantive resolution by voting against it. A permanent member's abstention does not count as a veto.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Does a permanent member's abstention count as a veto in the UN Security Council?

options.B: No, a permanent member's abstention does not count as a veto
options.C: Only if three or more permanent members abstain

questions.explanation: A permanent member's abstention does not count as a veto.

questions.subject: Current Affairs

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a principal organ of the United Nations?

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Where does the International Court of Justice fit within the UN system?

options.B: It is a subsidiary body of the Security Council
options.C: It is an autonomous specialised agency outside the UN system
options.D: It is part of the Secretariat

questions.explanation: The ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations. It settles legal disputes submitted by States and gives advisory opinions on legal questions referred by authorised UN organs and agencies.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the difference between a UN resolution and an international treaty?

options.B: A UN resolution is legally binding on all States; a treaty is only a political declaration

questions.explanation: A UN resolution is a formal decision or recommendation of a UN organ. A treaty is an agreement governed by international law and binds States that have consented to be bound, subject to its terms and entry-into-force rules.
